_schema.tier: primary = company filings, platform-published prices/take rates, ad-platform reported CPC/CPM, regulator data · survey = aggregated dataset with stated n and method (OpenView, ChartMogul, SaaS Capital, KeyBanc, ProfitWell) · secondary = practitioner posts, vendor blogs, roundups without stated n · method/derived = a formula or definition, not a source
_schema.confidence_from_tier: primary → medium (high only when the comparable is a direct competitor) · survey → medium · secondary → low
_schema.rule: Cite the entry id in the calibration basis. When research finds a fresher or higher-tier source for the same domain, add it as a new entry rather than overwriting; the newest highest-tier entry wins.
_schema.refresh: entries older than 24 months are flagged stale in the reality card; research step must try to replace them
_schema.archetype_rule: Before picking a churn/repeat benchmark, ask: does the product REPLACE an existing habit (email, spreadsheets, a paid tool) or CREATE a new behaviour (live audio, a new ritual, a novelty device)? New-behaviour products use the novelty entries, not the category entries — their retention has no floor from the old habit.
_schema.url_rule: primary and survey entries must carry a URL to the original; an entry whose figure was transcribed from a summary, or that rests on practitioner consensus without a URL, is tier secondary and carries verified:false — research must replace it before it is load-bearing

entries.unit: $ per FTE-month, fully loaded, mid-level engineer at seed-stage US startup
entries.source: Kruze Consulting Startup Compensation Guide (payroll data, 450+ funded startups)
entries.note: Source table: mid-level engineer base $90,000-$130,000 in 'other major tech hubs' and $100,000-$145,000 in San Francisco; entry-level $65k-$105k; senior $125k-$185k; Kruze: 'plan for total compensation costs to be about 25-35% higher than base salary'. Method: low = $90k x 1.25 / 12 = $9,375; high = $145k x 1.35 / 12 = $16,313. US only; Western Europe not covered by this source. Seed CEO salary $132k (2024 data), $153k (2026 report).

entries.unit: $ per FTE-month, senior software engineer, employer cost incl. on-costs (Ukraine low to Poland high)
entries.source: RemoteMore senior software engineer salary guide 2026 (aggregates Arc.dev, Lemon.io, Index.dev, Qubit Labs, GEOR, RemotifyEurope)
entries.note: Source table (senior, 5+ yrs, average annual remote comp): Poland $50,000-$100,000; Bulgaria $62,000-$95,000; Ukraine $32,000-$77,000; Romania $40,000-$76,000; 'full-time hires ... add 15-36% in employer costs depending on the country (Poland sits around 22%)'. Method: low = $32k x 1.15 / 12 = $3,067; high = $100k x 1.22 / 12 = $10,167. Mid-level engineers will sit below this band; source gives no n.

entries.unit: $ per FTE-month, software developer base salary (full-time), employer on-costs NOT included
entries.source: South (hireinsouth.com), Software Developer Rates by Country 2026
entries.note: Source table (annual full-time salary): Mexico $35,000-$75,000; Brazil $30,000-$70,000; Argentina $35,000-$80,000; Colombia $28,000-$60,000. Method: low = $28k / 12 = $2,333; high = $80k / 12 = $6,667. Vendor page (nearshore recruiter), no n; add ~15-40% employer on-costs for full-time hires depending on country.

entries.unit: $ cash per closed deal, prospecting tools only (events/travel excluded)
entries.source: Justin McKelvey, Founder-Led Sales guide (practitioner funnel targets); tool prices from same page
entries.note: Anecdotal, not a survey. Source targets: 20-40 outreach/week -> 5-10 discovery calls/week; 40-60% of calls qualified; 50-70% of qualified get a proposal; 30-50% of proposals close; tools: LinkedIn Sales Navigator $80/mo, Pipedrive $15/mo, HubSpot free. Method: conversations per closed deal = 1/(0.4..0.6 x 0.5..0.7 x 0.3..0.5) = 5-17; at 20-40 calls/month that is ~1.2-8 deals/month; tool spend ~$100-200/month -> $25-170 per deal. Events, travel and founder time are NOT in this figure; no survey with cash CAC per deal for founder-led sales was found in this pass. Founder time: ~10-15 hours per closed deal cited (Apollo, via blog.mean.ceo).

entries.unit: discovery calls per week, one founder spending 2-3 h/day on sales

entries.unit: % annual NRR, median to upper quartile, B2B SaaS >= $250k ARR
entries.source: ChartMogul / Kyle Poyar, SaaS Retention Report: The AI churn wave
entries.n: ~2,700 B2B SaaS, ~600 B2C SaaS, ~200 AI-native companies (ChartMogul data, 2025)
entries.note: Source: 'B2B SaaS ... median NRR was 82%. (The upper quartile was 97%.)'; AI-native GRR 40% / NRR 48%; AI-native >$250/mo plans 70% GRR / 85% NRR, <$50/mo plans 23% GRR / 32% NRR. Contrast with SaaS Capital 2025 (>$1M ARR, scale-ups): median NRR 101%. Use this entry for pre-$1M ARR companies.

entries.source: ChartMogul / Kyle Poyar, SaaS Retention Report: The AI churn wave
entries.note: Source: 'B2C is much less sticky with minimal upsell. The median NRR was only 49%'; 'AI-native companies had even worse GRR than B2C (40%) and comparable NRR (48%)'. Implies annual gross revenue churn of ~50 % for consumer subscription products at the median.

Method: annual expansion = NRR - GRR. B2C GRR is not printed by the source ('minimal upsell' -> lower bound 0); AI-native gap is 48 - 40 = 8 pts/yr -> (1.08)^(1/12)-1 = 0.64 %/mo, used as upper bound. Replaces the unverified expansion.consumer (0.5-1.5 %/mo), which overstated consumer upsell.

entries.unit: % monthly expansion, derived from NRR-GRR gap
entries.source: derived from SaaS Capital 2025 SaaS Retention Benchmarks for Private B2B Companies
entries.n: SaaS Capital annual survey, companies > $1M ARR (n not printed on page)
entries.note: Source page: ACV $25k-$50k median NRR 102%, top quartile 111%, lowest quartile 97%; overall survey median growth 24%. Research brief (linked PDF) reports overall median NRR 101% / GRR 91%. Method: annual expansion = NRR - GRR = ~6-20 pts (97-111 NRR vs ~91 GRR) -> (1.06)^(1/12)-1 = 0.49 %/mo to (1.20)^(1/12)-1 = 1.53 %/mo. Applies to scale-ups >$1M ARR; for pre-$1M ARR use nrr.b2b_saas.early.2025 (median NRR 82 %, i.e. net contraction).

entries.source: PitchBook Q3 2025 European VC Valuations Report, as summarised by Development Corporate (report itself gated)
entries.note: Summary of PitchBook Q3 2025 (https://pitchbook.com/news/reports/q3-2025-european-vc-valuations-report): 'pre-seed and seed companies saw the largest increase in median deal sizes - jumping 33.3% to €1.6 million' (vs ~€1.2M in 2024); pre-seed/seed median pre-money valuation €5.0M; UK & Ireland pre-seed/seed deal size €1.2M; with CVC participation €2.5M vs €1.4M without. Range = 2024 to Q3-2025 medians. PitchBook's own article (https://pitchbook.com/news/articles/bigger-checks-higher-price-tags-vc-valuations-rise-in-europe) gives all-stage median European deal €2.5M in H1 2025. Dealroom.co standardises Seed as $1-7M and Pre-Seed as >$250K (<$1M), and reports ~$2.5-3M of pre-Series-A capital in Europe (https://dealroom.co/startup-journey-europe/). No Europe-specific pre-seed-only median found.
